name: CrowdStrike Falcon
scope_notes: Public developer docs only; Falcon console documentation (IP allowlisting, audit event names, roles) requires login and is marked unknown. Next-Gen SIEM HEC needs a Next-Gen SIEM subscription; member_cid needs Flight Control.

controls.name: API scopes
controls.what: Each API client gets only the scopes selected for it; scopes can be changed later.
controls.setting: Support and resources > API Clients & Keys; PATCH /api-clients/entities/api-clients/v1

controls.name: ResetAPIClientSecret
controls.what: Issues a new secret for the client.

controls.name: oauth2RevokeToken
controls.what: Revokes a specific access token before its 30-minute expiry; needs the client's ID and secret.

controls.name: Regenerate Ingest token
controls.what: Regenerates the data connection ingest token.

controls_unknown: IP allowlisting for API clients: whether it exists, whether it applies to /oauth2/token or every API request (Falcon docs require login).
Whether deleting an API client or resetting its secret invalidates already-issued 30-minute tokens.
Audit event names for API client create/update/delete/secret reset and token issuance, and which field carries the client ID.
Whether ordinary API read calls are written to the audit log, and audit log retention.
Which Falcon roles can create API clients, and whether creation can require approval.
Whether a parent CID can be prevented from issuing member_cid tokens for specific child CIDs.
HEC ingest key expiry, IP restriction, and whether regeneration invalidates the old key immediately.
API rate limits (documented only inside Falcon).

credentials.name: OAuth2 API client (client ID and secret)

authentication.summary: An API client created in Support and resources > API Clients & Keys has a client ID, secret and selected API scopes. The pair is exchanged at POST /oauth2/token (regional base URL) for a 30-minute bearer token.

federation.details: No workload identity federation for API clients found in public docs.

ip_restriction.boundary: Falcon IP allowlisting docs are behind the Falcon console login; not verified.

lifetime.summary: Access token 30 min; client secret has no documented expiry

renewal.summary: Client requests a new token with the same ID and secret.

administration.summary: Create, update scopes, reset secret, or delete clients in the console or via /api-clients/entities/api-clients/v1 (Api Client Mgmt scope).
administration.conditions: Console role needed to manage API clients is documented only inside Falcon.

offboard.details: API clients are customer (CID)-level credentials created under API Clients & Keys, not user logins; docs do not say what happens if the creating user is removed.

inventory.details: GET /api-clients/queries/api-clients/v1 (GetAllAPIClientIdsForCustomer) plus GetAPIClients; also the console's API Clients & Keys page.

log_sources.name: Falcon audit logs (Audit API)
log_sources.notes: Query via POST /audit-logs/queries/queryjobs/v1 (scope Audit: READ); filters include actor_id, actor_ip, actor_type, user_agent, action. Retention not public.

log_sources.name: Event Streams
log_sources.notes: Streaming API (scope Event streams: READ); audit event types not verified from public docs.

credential_id_fields.notes: Whether this holds the API client ID for API actions is not documented.

anomaly_cues: New API client with write scopes (Real time response (admin), Hosts, API Client Mgmt)
Secret reset on an existing client
API calls from unfamiliar actor_ip or user_agent

containment.steps: Delete the API client or reset its secret; revoke known tokens with POST /oauth2/revoke.
containment.notes: Tokens last up to 30 min if not revoked.

calls.reveals: Event stream URLs for continuous data

unknown: No documented whoami for the API client itself

detections.title: Crowdstrike API Key Created
detections.detects: A Falcon API client (client ID and secret) was created.

credentials.name: Flight Control (MSSP) parent API client acting on a child CID (member_cid)

authentication.summary: An API client in a Flight Control parent CID can request a token with member_cid to act on a child CID.

lifetime.summary: Same 30-min token as other API clients

renewal.summary: New token per child CID with the parent's client credentials.

administration.summary: Managed in the parent CID; parent can list linked child CIDs via /mssp/queries/children/v1.
administration.conditions: Falcon Flight Control subscription (documented in console).

offboard.details: Parent-CID API client credential, not a user login.

inventory.details: Same API client listing (GET /api-clients/queries/api-clients/v1) in the parent CID.

usage.api: POST /audit-logs/queries/queryjobs/v1 with cid=[<child CID>] (and actor_id); poll GET /audit-logs/entities/queryjobs/v1?id=; read GET /audit-logs/entities/queryjob-results/v1?id=

log_sources.name: Falcon audit logs (Audit API)
log_sources.notes: Has a cid filter; whether child CID logs show parent client actions is not documented.

anomaly_cues: Parent client tokens minted for many child CIDs

containment.steps: Delete or reset the parent API client.

unknown: Child-side visibility of parent API use

credentials.name: Next-Gen SIEM HEC data connector API key (ingest token)

authentication.summary: Creating an HEC/HTTP Event Data Connector produces an API key and URL used by log shippers to send events into Next-Gen SIEM.

lifetime.summary: Token has an expires_at timestamp; default and max not documented

administration.summary: Next-Gen SIEM > Data ingestion > Data connectors.
administration.conditions: Falcon Next-Gen SIEM subscription; Administrator or Connector Manager.

offboard.details: The key belongs to the data connector, shown on the connector's detail page.

inventory.details: GET /ngsiem/combined/connections/v1 lists data connections; console page Next-Gen SIEM > Data ingestion > Data connectors.

usage.ui: Next-Gen SIEM > Data ingestion > Data connectors > <connector> > Show events (or Advanced Event Search filtered on the connector's #connector tag)

log_sources.name: Next-Gen SIEM events tagged #connector
log_sources.notes: Ingested data can be filtered by the connector tag; key-use audit not documented.

anomaly_cues: Unexpected events or volume on a connector (log injection)

containment.steps: Regenerate the ingest token or delete the connector.
containment.notes: Regenerating the ingest token invalidates the previous one; timing not stated.

unknown: Audit events for connector key regeneration
Ingest key is write-only per docs reviewed; read capability not documented
